records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin/stablecoin financial infrastructure and payments API
records.Concise description: Financial infrastructure platform using Bitcoin, Lightning, stablecoins and local rails for cross-border business payments, wallets, payouts and APIs with product-dependent custody.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitnob positions its current business platform as infrastructure connecting African and global businesses to bank/mobile-money and crypto rails. Bitcoin/Lightning remain part of its payment architecture, while current products also use stablecoins and fiat-connected services. Its wallet/payment modes are not uniformly self-custodial: hosted business balances and custodial wallet flows coexist with some self-custodial capabilities, so each public custody statement must be tied to the specific product path.
records.Launch / history: Founded as an African Bitcoin-focused financial service and expanded into business APIs, cross-border payments and multi-rail infrastructure.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is a meaningful example of Bitcoin/Lightning being used as part of regional and global payment infrastructure rather than only direct merchant checkout.
records.Verification basis: An official help article edited April 29, 2026 and current business/developer surfaces verify active financial infrastructure and cross-border payment operations.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not use one custody label for all Bitnob products.
Do not turn current corridor, currency or country coverage into timeless copy; it changes with partners and regulation.
Stablecoins/local rails are contextual to Bitnob's Bitcoin payment infrastructure, not grounds for broad stablecoin coverage in PAYMENTS.

records.Entity / project type: regional Bitcoin/Lightning payment and remittance company
records.Concise description: Philippines-focused payments company using Bitcoin and Lightning for merchant acceptance and cross-border money movement.
records.Deeper researched summary: Pouch.ph positions itself as a Philippines payment company that connects merchant and cross-border flows through Bitcoin/Lightning while operating within local payment regulation. Its public current site supports the inclusion case, but detailed technical custody, liquidity and settlement architecture is not sufficiently documented in the accessible first-party material to support stronger universal claims.
records.Launch / history: Built in the early 2020s around Lightning merchant acceptance and remittance/payment connectivity in the Philippines.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It illustrates a regional payments model where Lightning can operate underneath local-currency merchant and cross-border use cases.
Important technical or cultural characte: Custody and settlement architecture requires product-specific verification
records.Verification basis: Current first-party site verifies continued operation and Bitcoin/Lightning payment positioning, but accessible technical/legal product detail is incomplete enough to retain MEDIUM confidence.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not publish an unqualified custodial/non-custodial label until the current product flow is directly documented.
Reverify licensing, settlement currencies, supported corridors and merchant terms before public copy.
If later evidence shows the canonical product is primarily a wallet rather than payment network, WALLETS may be the better home.

records.Entity / project type: custodial Bitcoin/Lightning access and payment service
records.Concise description: Custodial Bitcoin and Lightning service designed to let users send and receive sats over USSD and other low-bandwidth channels without requiring a smartphone data connection.
records.Deeper researched summary: Machankura links a custodial Bitcoin/Lightning wallet account to a phone number and PIN and issues a Lightning Address, enabling payments through USSD in supported markets. Its own FAQ explicitly calls the service fully custodial. The distinctive PAYMENTS reason is not 'another Lightning wallet' but access infrastructure: it adapts Bitcoin payments to feature-phone and low-connectivity environments.
records.Launch / history: Started in the early 2020s as a USSD-based Bitcoin service for African users and expanded access methods while retaining low-connectivity payments as its defining design.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It demonstrates how payment connectivity and user interface constraints can matter as much as the underlying Lightning rail in regions with limited smartphone/data penetration.
records.Verification basis: Current 2026 first-party FAQ explicitly documents the fully custodial model, USSD operation and Lightning Address/payment behavior.
Research notes / uncertainties: The FAQ and other current surfaces may show different counts/lists of supported countries; do not publish a static country count without rechecking.
Do not imply USSD itself is the payment rail; it is the access channel to a custodial Bitcoin/Lightning service.

records.Entity / project type: crypto commerce / gift-card and digital-goods marketplace
records.Concise description: Commerce platform that lets users spend Bitcoin and Lightning on gift cards, phone refills, eSIMs and other digital purchasing bridges.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitrefill is not merely a merchant that happens to accept Bitcoin: converting BTC/Lightning into broad merchant gift-card and prepaid access has been its core product since 2014. Current checkout supports Bitcoin and Lightning alongside other assets. Bitrefill is the commerce counterparty for purchases rather than a generic processor that routes payment to third-party merchants, so its trust model is principally fulfillment/counterparty risk rather than custody of a continuing Bitcoin balance.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2014 around using Bitcoin for mobile refills and later expanded to a large gift-card/digital-goods commerce catalog with Lightning support.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It became a durable bridge between Bitcoin spending and merchants that do not natively accept Bitcoin, making it more structurally important than an ordinary Bitcoin-accepting store.
Important technical or cultural characte: No requirement that downstream brand natively accept Bitcoin
Fulfillment/counterparty model rather than merchant-processing infrastructure
records.Verification basis: Current official commerce site verifies Bitcoin and Lightning as active payment methods and a long-running commerce-spend role.
Research notes / uncertainties: Catalog size, country coverage, supported brands and payment assets are time-sensitive and should not be copied as timeless statistics.
Bitrefill is included as a durable Bitcoin-spend bridge; ordinary merchants accepting BTC are deliberately excluded from this canon.
